question: Does current sibling Codex source confirm that a 30-second device-code HTTP operation deadline and the proposed timeout-versus-cancellation mapping match the intended authentication contract?
rationale: OpenClaw policy makes direct Codex source inspection a hard gate, and this provider-auth change alters user-visible failure timing even though its implementation and proof otherwise look sound.

options.title: Verify contract, then merge
options.body: Inspect the current Codex device-login client, rebase this PR, and merge if its timeout and cancellation semantics agree with this implementation.

options.title: Revise timeout semantics
options.body: Request a different deadline or error mapping if current Codex behavior establishes a materially different provider contract.

recommendation.title: Verify contract, then merge
recommendation.body: Inspect the current Codex device-login client, rebase this PR, and merge if its timeout and cancellation semantics agree with this implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their feature-history connection to the device-code login path makes them the strongest available owner for its intended timeout and cancellation behavior.
